arguments.value: William D. Quarles, Jr. is a former United States District Judge for the District of Maryland who served from 2003 until his retirement in 2016. Born in Baltimore in 1948, he earned an A.A. from Community College of Baltimore, a B.S. from the University of Maryland, and a J.D. from the Catholic University of America’s Columbus School of Law. After clerking for Judge Joseph C. Howard, he practiced privately and served as an assistant U.S. attorney before returning to private practice in Baltimore and later serving as an associate judge on the Maryland Circuit Court in Baltimore City. Nominated to the federal bench by President George W. Bush and confirmed by the Senate in 2003, he brought decades of legal and judicial experience to the court.
